entities.summary: Jerome Clarke Hunsaker was an American naval officer and aeronautical engineer, born in Creston, Iowa, and educated at the U.S. Naval Academy and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology. His work with Gustav Eiffel outside Paris led to the first wind tunnel in the US at MIT. He was instrumental in developing a weather reporting and airway navigation. Hunsaker was also pivotal in establishing the theoretical and scientific study of aerodynamics in the United States. And he was primarily responsible for the design and construction of the Navy-Curtiss airplane (NC-4) that accomplished the first transatlantic flight, and the first successful shipboard fighter.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Hunsaker's work on aerodynamics and navigation led to the development of the Navy-Curtiss airplane (NC-4), which accomplished the first transatlantic flight in 1919. This achievement marked a significant milestone in aviation history.
